data.narrative:
Neuralink is a private-stage AI & Software company that has raised $1.3B+ to date. The target operates within a fragmented peer universe comprising 1 public comparable (Palantir Technologies, ticker PLTR) and 8 private peers including Scale AI, Figure AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. However, this comp set presents material limitations for valuation synthesis.

The Peer-Median method—typically the foundation of triangulated analysis—is not applicable here. Neuralink's specific stage, scale, and business model characteristics yielded insufficient narrow-filter matches: only 1 same-stage peer was identified, with 0 adjacent-stage and 0 similar-tier comparables available. Applying an all-sector median across the 12 broader AI & Software peers would introduce unacceptable distortion given the heterogeneity in business models, revenue structures, and development timelines within that universe. Standard public-market multiples derived from PLTR alone are similarly unreliable as a standalone anchor given fundamental differences in maturity and capital intensity.

This analysis cannot support a point valuation or narrow range. A defensible assessment would require either (1) expanded access to transaction data from nearer-peer late-stage rounds, (2) explicit revenue or milestone-based modeling if available, or (3) explicit acknowledgment that Neuralink's capital intensity, long development horizon, and founder-driven risk profile place it outside conventional VC valuation frameworks. Further diligence on recent Series funding terms and comparable medical-device AI ventures may narrow the uncertainty.
